title: A Knight Needs a Sidekick
boundary: Don Quixote Part I chapter 1 only, John Ormsby (1885). Prior edition/range retained; current classroom translation not independently verified.

vocabulary.source: David’s CORE_VOCAB_BY_WEEK.txt; local schedule, not a live Canvas check

storyCircle.you: Student arrives as themself, seeking an answer to one question.
storyCircle.need: Help a would-be hero without losing sight of what help requires.
storyCircle.go: Write one question; jump through the journal and land in laundry.
storyCircle.search: Choose equipment, discover Quixote’s motives and negotiate loyalty.
storyCircle.find: Heroic names and a repaired helmet seem to complete his preparation.
storyCircle.take: A runaway cart forces the student to prioritize a person or books; equipment and saved chance affect losses.
storyCircle.return: Recover the books, decide how to tell the rescue, and reach the journal door.
storyCircle.change: Use evidence without erasing sympathy; knowledge quiz remains separate from fortune.

motives.student: Wants to be useful as a temporary sidekick; chooses how to balance approval, honesty and practical help.
motives.Quixote: Wants to act in a world made larger by his books. Believes heroic models and names can give him a purposeful life. Questions feel like dismissal; damage to books touches both financial cost and cherished hope.

adaptation: Temporary sidekick, all dialogue, courtyard mishap and magic are authored additions, not canonical incidents. Student is not Sancho. No later chapter is retold, no lasting canonical reform is claimed.
learningTargets: Evidence and inference from the sale of land for books
Diction, close reading and parody in the untested helmet
Intertextuality in the Amadis naming model
Declared identities versus ability or another person’s agreement
characters: Shared versioned Mr. Hepting manga rig
Quixote recipe: shared cartoon-v1, adult/angular face, grey hair and beard, generic brown tunic; not exact period costume
